topic: A review of the clinical evidence for complementary and alternative therapies in Parkinson's disease

sources.title: A review of the clinical evidence for complementary and alternative therapies in Parkinson's disease
sources.authors: Bega D, Gonzalez-Latapi P, Zadikoff C, Simuni T.

findings.finding: Dance is specifically recommended as an enjoyable and challenging activity for patients to engage in.
findings.quote: patients should be encouraged to be as active as possible and engage with others in enjoyable and challenging activities such as dance, music therapy, and yoga.

findings.finding: Mind-body practices that combine physical activity with relaxation and mindfulness are beneficial for patients.
findings.quote: mind-body interventions such as Tai Chi that incorporate relaxation and mindfulness with physical activity should be routinely encouraged as well.

principle: Engaging in enjoyable, challenging, and social mind-body activities like dance is recommended as a beneficial complement to standard care for managing Parkinson's disease.
for_the_teacher: Design dance sequences that are both enjoyable and mentally challenging to keep the learner engaged.
Incorporate moments of mindfulness or relaxation into the dance lesson to support a holistic mind-body approach.
Encourage the learner to view their dance practice as an active, empowering part of their overall health management.
when_it_does_not_apply: The source notes that while these activities are encouraged, there is limited evidence regarding their ability to slow or stop the progression of Parkinson's disease.
